verdict.rationale: The docs list 'tunneled MCP servers' as a first-party tool source alongside custom remote servers, and say tool logs cover tunneled servers. That points to a built-in way to bridge non-deployed servers into the platform as managed connections. However, the evidence is only a passing mention: there is no setup guide, and nothing confirms the tunnel targets a locally running process or how it is managed. The remote-source proxy (gram-docs-13/14) needs a reachable URL, so it is not evidence of local bridging. Missing for 10: documented tunnel setup flow, explicit confirmation of local-process bridging without deployment, details on how the tunneled connection is managed, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can bridge a locally running MCP server into the platform as a managed remote connection without deploying it

citations.quote: Every tool source in the project in one place: OpenAPI documents, TypeScript functions, third-party catalog servers, custom remote MCP servers, and tunneled MCP servers.
the raw execution log for every tool call the platform observes across hosted MCP servers, tunneled and shadow MCP servers, skills, and local tools
